Court filings detail attempts to avoid being served in lawsuit over threats to Parton's legacy.

Actual Article Body:
What This Story Is About

Why It Matters

What Happens Next

For Context

Catch Up

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - A judge has extended a temporary restraining order against Dolly Parton’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, after new court filings detailed how he tried to avoid being served a lawsuit accusing him of threatening to destroy the late country icon’s legacy.

New court filings from the estate, submitted Monday, claim Seaver avoided being served court papers with a “no trespassing” sign, as well as barbed wire and yellow caution tape placed around the stairs leading to his front door.

Seaver is asking for more time to get an attorney before a hearing that was scheduled for Oct. 9.

Parton’s estate asked the judge to deny that request and to extend the temporary restraining order, which was set to expire Thursday.

A judge granted the extension of the temporary restraining order Tuesday and rescheduled the next court appearance for Oct. 20.
